minutes_text:
CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Video Teleconference
  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison Property Owners Task Force Committee
  Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Thursday, January 25, 2024
  10:00 AM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  January 25, 2024 / 10:00 AM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Councilmember Lili Bosse, Councilmember Sharona Nazarian, Assistant
  City Manager Ryan Gohlich, Community Outreach Manager Magdalena
  Davis, Principal Planner Ray Balderas, Chamber of Commerce President
  and CEO Todd Johnson, , Chamber of Commerce Director of Economic
  Development & Government Affairs Brittany Ganson

  1) Public Comment:

  None

  2) Welcome and Introductions:
  a. All people in attendance introduced themselves.

  3) Continued Item from Task Force Previous Meeting: Outdoor Dining
  a. Presentation from Ray Balderas.
  i. The Open Air Dining Ordinance was approved by Council in December and
  officially adopted on January 11, 2024.
  ii. The city is working with businesses to get existing open air dining facilities
  approved.
  iii. Applicants for the permanent open air dining program can apply online,
  with the program going into effect on March 1, 2024.
  iv. The ordinance includes both outdoor dining and “Parklets” which utilize
  meter space on roads.
  v. The city is cooperating with Pasadena with the launch of their open air
  dining program.
  vi. Palo Alto and Oakland have also reached out to Beverly Hills about the
  open air dining program, specifically concerning the kit of parts for the
  parklets, which both cities see as a model.
  vii. Parklets were designed to ensure the safety of occupants from car crashes
  up to at least 25 MPH, and are specifically zoned for areas with that speed
  limit.
  viii. The costs to purchase a parklet start around $60,000.
 Highlights for January 25, 2024
Property Owners Task Force Committee

  ix. Parklet fees have three tiers depending on their location.
  x. If people want to deviate from the set criteria for parklets, they will need
  authorization from the planning commission and/or the architectural
  commission.
  xi. March 1st is the deadline for applying for a glide path to upgrade existing
  parklets to meet new city standards. Parklets who have applied to be a part
  of the open air dining program will be allowed to continue to operate
  existing parklet structures throughout the duration of the application and
  upgrade process.
  xii. Councilmember Nazarian made a request to the Assistant City Manager to
  investigate over the removal of “Curbside Pick Up” parking signs after the
  business closes for the day so the spots can be used for parking.
  xiii. Curbside pick up spots are regularly used by uber and food delivery drivers
  for employees of the building, who may otherwise block the alley or ADA
  spaces.
  xiv. All outdoor dining spaces need to be approved by the city but specific
  parklet standards only apply to parklets on the street, not to privately owned
  parking lots.

  4) Information Sharing and Discussion
  a. Businesses have expressed their thanks and support for the new crosswalks
  installed in places such as North Camden.
  b. Proposal for a pedestrian crossing between Wilshire and Charleville on South
  Beverly.
  c. Proposal to extend rooftop dining from the Triangle to South Beverly or to allow for
  businesses to utilize the top floor of mixed use development.
  d. Several tenants are migrating from North Beverly Drive to South Beverly Drive,
  which raises the future prospect of formally attaching South Beverly to the Triangle.

  5) Future Agenda Item(s) Discussion:
  a. There was a proposal to have the President and CEO of LA SEC Kathryn
  Schloessman have a presentation at the next meeting in March which received a
  positive response.

  6) Adjournment:
  Date / Time: January 25, 2024 / 11:05 AM
